title: Taking the Floor and Interrupting Politely

sections.content:
You know the polite imperfect (*quería pedirle*) from B2 Unit 2 and formal institutional register from B2 Unit 14. In a moderated debate or panel, interrupting without sounding aggressive relies on softening verbs in the imperfect and formal *usted* turn-management formulas.

The polite imperfect distances a request or intervention from the immediate moment: *Quería añadir un dato*, *Deseaba intervenir brevemente*, *Venía a señalar ese punto*. Paired with formal *usted* formulas — *Si me permite intervenir*, *Con el debido respeto*, *Si me cede la palabra un segundo* — it lets you claim the floor while acknowledging the moderator and the other speaker.

Notice the verb pairs for managing turns: *pedir la palabra* (to ask to speak), *tomar la palabra* (to take the floor), *ceder la palabra* (to yield the floor) and *retomar* (to resume a point).

sections.title: Polite floor-taking formulas
rows: Quería añadir una precisión sobre ese punto.
Si me permite intervenir, quisiera retomar ese dato.
Yielding or asking for the floor
Le cedo la palabra, pero le pido brevedad.
Con el debido respeto, discrepo de esa lectura.

items.spanish: Disculpe que interrumpa, pero quería añadir una precisión sobre los datos.
items.english: Excuse me for interrupting, but I wanted to add a clarification on the figures.

items.spanish: Si me permite tomar la palabra, deseo retomar el tema anterior.
items.english: If you allow me to take the floor, I wish to return to the previous topic.

items.spanish: El moderador pidió brevedad antes de ceder la palabra a la invitada.
items.english: The moderator asked for brevity before yielding the floor to the guest.

items.spanish: Quería pedir la palabra para responder a la última alusión.
items.english: I wanted to ask for the floor to respond to the latest allusion.

sections.content: Do not confuse the polite imperfect (*Quería añadir...* = 'I would like / I wanted to add...') with a past action that is over. In formal debates, keep *usted* consistent throughout the turn (*Si me permite... le agradezco...*, never mixing *si me permites* with *le cede*).
